# M3 · Viewing: progressive hints

<!-- GENERATED by tools/build.py from content/*.yaml. Edit the YAML, not this file. -->
Open one level at a time. **Hint 1** gives the conceptual direction, **Hint 2** the SQL technique, **Hint 3** the query structure, and the final level is in [`solutions/`](../solutions/).

## M3-E01 · A view that hides the joins

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

A view is `CREATE VIEW name AS <any SELECT>;`

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

Reuse the three-table JOIN from M0-E09.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`CREATE VIEW "longlist" AS SELECT "name", "title" FROM "authors" JOIN "authored" ON ... JOIN "books" ON ...;`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M3.md#m3-e01).

## M3-E02 · Fernanda's books, now in one line

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

You can query a view exactly like a table.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

It already has a `name` and a `title` column.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`SELECT "title" FROM "longlist" WHERE "name" = 'Fernanda Melchor';`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M3.md#m3-e02).

## M3-E03 · The average_book_ratings view

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Ratings live in `ratings`, but title and year live in `books`, so you need a JOIN.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

Group by the book so each book becomes one row.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`SELECT "book_id", "title", "year", ROUND(AVG("rating"), 2) AS "rating" FROM "ratings" JOIN "books" ON "ratings"."book_id" = "books"."id" GROUP BY "book_id"`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M3.md#m3-e03).

## M3-E04 · A temporary view built on a view

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

A view can be built on top of another view.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

`CREATE TEMPORARY VIEW name AS <query>;` The query aggregates per year with AVG and ROUND.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`SELECT "year", ROUND(AVG("rating"), 2) AS "rating" FROM "average_book_ratings" GROUP BY "year"`, wrapped in the CREATE TEMPORARY VIEW.

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M3.md#m3-e04).

## M3-E05 · The same analysis with a CTE

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

`WITH name AS ( query ) SELECT ... FROM name ...;`

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

The CTE body is the per-book average query from M3-E03, without CREATE VIEW.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`WITH "average_book_ratings" AS (SELECT ... GROUP BY "book_id") SELECT "year", ROUND(AVG("rating"), 2) AS "rating" FROM "average_book_ratings" GROUP BY "year";`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M3.md#m3-e05).

## M3-E06 · Partition the books by year

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

A partition is a filtered SELECT saved as a view.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

A name that is just digits must be quoted, as `"2022"`.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`CREATE VIEW "2022" AS SELECT "id", "title" FROM "books" WHERE "year" = 2022;`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M3.md#m3-e06).

## M3-E07 · Try to update a view

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Write the UPDATE against the view's name.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

`UPDATE "2021" SET ... WHERE ...;`

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`UPDATE "2021" SET "title" = 'The Minor Detail' WHERE "title" = 'Minor Detail';`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M3.md#m3-e07).

## M3-E08 · Fix the typo where the data lives

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

The view only *reads* from another table.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

Change the underlying `books` row.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`UPDATE "books" SET "title" = 'The Minor Detail' WHERE "title" = 'Minor Detail';`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M3.md#m3-e08).

## M3-E09 · An anonymized view for analysts

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Leave out the real `rider` column, which is personally identifiable information (PII).

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

A literal in the SELECT list produces that value on every row: `'anonymous' AS "rider"`.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`CREATE VIEW "analysis" AS SELECT "id", "origin", "destination", 'anonymous' AS "rider" FROM "rides";`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M3.md#m3-e09).

## M3-E10 · current_collections, a view over soft deletes

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Filter on the flag, and don't expose it.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

`WHERE "deleted" = 0`

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`CREATE VIEW "current_collections" AS SELECT "id", "title", "accession_number", "acquired" FROM "collections" WHERE "deleted" = 0;`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M3.md#m3-e10).

## M3-E11 · INSTEAD OF DELETE, turning a delete into a soft delete

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

`CREATE TRIGGER "delete" INSTEAD OF DELETE ON "current_collections" FOR EACH ROW BEGIN ... END;`

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

`OLD."id"` is the id of the view row being deleted.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

Body: `UPDATE "collections" SET "deleted" = 1 WHERE "id" = OLD."id";` Don't forget the WHERE.

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M3.md#m3-e11).

## M3-E12 · INSTEAD OF INSERT ... WHEN, re-acquiring a deleted item

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Triggers can be conditional: `FOR EACH ROW WHEN <condition> BEGIN ... END;`

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

The condition: `NEW."accession_number" IN (SELECT "accession_number" FROM "collections")`.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

Body: `UPDATE "collections" SET "deleted" = 0 WHERE "accession_number" = NEW."accession_number";`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M3.md#m3-e12).

## M3-E13 · Assigned: INSTEAD OF INSERT for genuinely new items

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Same shape as `insert_when_exists`, with the opposite condition.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

`WHEN NEW."accession_number" NOT IN (SELECT "accession_number" FROM "collections")`

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

Body: `INSERT INTO "collections" ("title", "accession_number", "acquired") VALUES (NEW."title", NEW."accession_number", NEW."acquired");`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M3.md#m3-e13).

## D3-01 · A trailing comma after the CTE

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

What does a comma after a CTE announce?

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

Another CTE follows. Here there is none.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

Remove the comma after `)`.

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M3.md#d3-01).

## D3-02 · The soft-delete trigger that hid everything

<details><summary>Hint 1 · direction</summary>

Which rows does the UPDATE inside the trigger touch?

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 2 · technique</summary>

The trigger runs once per deleted view row. Use that row's identity.

</details>

<details><summary>Hint 3 · structure</summary>

`WHERE "id" = OLD."id"`

</details>

Final: [solution](../solutions/M3.md#d3-02).
